lectures.title: Indus Valley Civilization: discovery, extent, economy and trade

items: **Earliest known urban civilization:** the Indus Valley Civilization.
**Largest IVC / Harappan site in India:** Rakhigarhi.
Saw pottery, tools & seal; significance not recognized
**Ropar** is the first Harappan site excavated in independent India.

parts.t: Extent: the boundary sites and outposts
items: **Eastern boundary of Harappan culture:** Alamgirpur (Meerut, U.P.; river Hindon).
**Western boundary of Harappan culture:** Sutkagendor (Baluchistan, Pakistan).
**Shortughai (Afghanistan):** Harappan trade outpost; associated with lapis lazuli.
**Manda (Jammu & Kashmir):** on the Chenab; procurement of Himalayan wood (timber).
**Occupations of the Harappans:** agriculture + trade + crafts.
**Lothal:** Harappan port city / port-town in Gujarat on the Gulf of Khambhat, on the Bhogava River; evidence of dock/port; dockyard; maritime trade with West Asia.
**Earliest public water tank:** the Great Bath, Mohenjo-daro.

lectures.title: Indus Valley sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro and the major cities

items: **Location:** on the river Ravi; Punjab, Pakistan.
**Most important findings:** Cemetery R-37 + Granary + Unicorn seal.
**Burials:** Cemetery R-37, Cemetery H, coffin burial, graveyard.
**Grain:** wheat + barley, found in a wooden mortar.
**Objects:** dice, copper scale, copper mirror, unicorn seal.
**First artefact:** a stone seal with unicorn + inscription.
**Most important findings:** Great Bath + Dancing Girl + Priest-King + Pashupati.
**Great Bath:** probably for ritual bathing; the earliest public water tank.
**Large building:** possibly of a high official / high priest / college of priests.
**Roads:** excellent road planning; main road about 9.15 m; roads intersect at right angles.
Horse teeth; cotton cloth; skeletons in wells; ivory weight balance
**Chanhudaro** is the only major Harappan city without a citadel.
**Identity:** bead industry; bead-making factory and furnace (excavated by E.J.H. Mackay, 1935–36).
**Objects:** lipsticks, ornamented elephant, toys, ink pot, carts with seated driver, phase-cut bricks.
**Famous for:** the dockyard; brick basin; port/trading centre; trade with West Asia.
**Most important findings:** Dockyard + Rice + Fire altars.
**Craftsmen:** metal workers, shell ornament makers, bead makers.
**Other findings:** rice husk, fire altars, horse figurine, ship model, Persian seal, painted jars, shop.
**Also found:** graveyard, three double burials, ivory weight balance, copper dog.
**Kalibangan** has the earliest excavated evidence of a ploughed agricultural field.
**Associated with:** ploughed field; fire altars; terracotta plough.
**Other findings:** Mesopotamian seals, toy-cart wheels, wooden plough, copper ox, camel bones.
**Urban planning:** a 3-part city with three divisions: Citadel + Middle Town + Lower Town.
**Water management:** huge reservoirs, rock-cut reservoirs, water storage, dams, embankments; an advanced water-harnessing system; Great Bath.
**Other findings:** stadium-like structure; special cemetery structures.

lectures.title: Indus Valley sites: the smaller sites and their signature finds

items: **Identity:** largest IVC site in India; a major Harappan urban site.
**Findings:** granary, cemetery, drains, terracotta bricks, double burials; provincial-capital character in the material.
**Findings:** terracotta replica of plough (toy plough); Mother Goddess figurines; large quantity of barley grains.
**Location:** Kurukshetra, Haryana; river Saraswati; excavated by J.P. Joshi.
**Importance:** Harappan / Late Harappan site; Late Harappan + PGW association. No distinctive artefact is identified.
**Location:** Haryana. **Finding:** plant remains; earliest evidence of garlic.

parts.t: Punjab and Jammu & Kashmir: Ropar and Manda
items: **River:** Sutlej. First Harappan site excavated in independent India.
**Findings:** stone + soil buildings; dog buried with humans (dog burial); inscribed steatite seal; Indus pictographs; oval pit burials.
**Importance:** procurement of Himalayan wood (timber); the wood was transported downstream to other Harappan towns.

parts.t: Uttar Pradesh: Alamgirpur, Hulas, Sinauli, Mandi
items: **Location:** Meerut, U.P.; river Hindon; eastern boundary of Harappan culture.
**Findings:** terracotta bead-like object coated with gold; evidence of cloth; utensils with triangle, peacock and squirrel impressions.
**Findings:** handmade pottery; wheel-made pottery; geometric designs; naturalistic black-painted designs; chert blades; bone points.
**Location:** Baghpat, U.P. **Finding:** 116 graves, mostly primary human burials, in North–South orientation (N-S burials).
**Grave goods:** some graves contained animal bones, gold, copper and bangles.
**Location:** Muzaffarnagar, U.P. **Finding:** jewellery/treasure hoard of the Late Harappan period; discovery in June 2000.

parts.t: Gujarat and Maharashtra: Surkotada, Rangpur and others
items: **Surkotada (Kachchh, Gujarat):** horse bones and pot burials; the horse-related evidence is debated.
**Rangpur (Saurashtra, Gujarat):** Late Harappan; agricultural evidence of rice, bajra and sorghum.
**Daimabad (Maharashtra; river Pravara):** bronze objects, including a bronze chariot, bronze buffalo and bronze sculptures.
**Sutkagendor (Baluchistan, Pakistan):** western boundary of Harappan culture; clay bangles.

lectures.title: Indus Valley Civilization: religion and rituals

items: **Mother Goddess:** Harappan worship / Harappan religion; terracotta female figurines.
**Fire / Yagya rituals:** associated with the Indus Valley Civilization.
**IVC fire rituals:** at the Rajasthan & Gujarat sites.
**Burial rituals:** associated with the Indus Valley Civilization.
**Boghaz-Koi inscription** mentions the Vedic gods Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatya.
Northern India / land occupied by Aryans
**Battle of 10 Kings / Dasharajnya:** Sudas vs a Confederacy of 10 Kings; leader Sudas; decisive victory of Sudas; mentioned in the Rigveda.
**Aghanya:** the cow; not worthy of being killed.
**Metals of the Rigvedic Aryans:** gold + silver + copper.
**Iron Age in India:** Later Vedic period, c. 1000 BC; iron spread in North India in 1000–600 BC.
Chief priest / religious adviser to the king
Head of the village / village-level authority
Priest responsible for the practical/manual aspects of sacrifice
Teacher who taught Veda/Vedanga as a profession

parts.t: The four Vedas and the Brahmanas
items: Rituals; Yajna / sacrifice; Vedic ritual procedure
**Brahmanical / Vedic religion:** its texts are the Vedas; the Vedic ritual tradition is in the Brahmanas.
**Early Vedic religion:** nature worship + yajnas; Rigvedic religion was polytheistic.
Vedic deity / warrior; Purandara → destroyer of forts; most powerful deity
**Rita:** Vedic concept of the cosmic / natural order.
**Upanishads:** philosophical literature; a philosophy for all times and for all.
**Basic philosophy:** universal approach; does not oppose any school of thought, religion or scriptural interpretation.
Self; concept of self: core of the self, not body or mind
Liberation; first discussed in the Upanishads
**Life–death cycle:** the continuous cycle of life and death is not the actual aim of the human soul.
**Katha Upanishad:** Yama + Nachiketa; conversation on death and what lies beyond it.
**Mundakopanishad:** the national motto, Satyameva Jayate → Truth alone triumphs.
**Brihadaranyaka Upanishad:** the spiritual maxim Tamasoma Jyotirgamaya → Lead from darkness to light / ignorance to truth.
**Vedanta:** philosophical system; Upanishads + Brahma Sutra + Bhagavad Gita.
**Vedanta, literal meaning:** end of the Vedas / climax of Vedic ideology.
**Prasthanatrayi:** the foundations of Vedanta: Upanishads + Brahma Sutra + Bhagavad Gita.
**Yoga:** philosophical tradition; descriptions found in the Upanishads, Mahabharata, Bhagavad Gita, Jain & Buddhist texts.
**Patanjali:** later explained Yoga as a compact philosophical theory → Patanjali Darshan.
